$comment: The toolchain every build and every recorded figure assumes, one set per platform. Metal has no container image to pin, as Charlotte pinned emsdk's, and the RTX 3090 Ti's machine is the user's own, so the versions are pinned here instead and tools/check_toolchain.py compares them with the machine's at configure time, its platform's set alone: the compilers CMake resolved, and on macOS the SDK, the Metal compiler and Xcode, and CMake, whose version decides the compile lines; a mismatch stops the build. To move a pin, change this file in its own commit and rerun the tests: a new compiler can change what the shaders or the core compute.

macos.$lint: The formatter and the static checks, LLVM's, which the build does not run: make format, format-check and tidy, and clangd in the editor (docs/process/workflow.md). The formatter's output depends on its version, so it is pinned with the others; tools/check_toolchain.py --lint checks these alone, and only those targets ask it to, so a machine without them still builds. brew install llvm.

linux.$comment: The RTX 3090 Ti's machine, Ubuntu 24.04 (docs/research/2026-10-19-cuda-backend.md): Ubuntu's clang 18 for C and C++, Ubuntu's CMake, CUDA 13.2's nvcc for the kernels, and NVIDIA's driver, which runs them and is OptiX's runtime.
linux.$lint: LLVM's own release of 21.1.8, the Mac's version, unpacked to ~/.local/opt/llvm-21.1.8 (docs/process/workflow.md); tools/check_toolchain.py --lint checks these alone.
